security_audit.summary: All 58 static findings are false positives caused by documentation examples, placeholder Azure URLs, environment-aware snippets, and read-only diagnostics. One semantic issue remains: SKILL.md uses authority-framing language that can encourage agents to treat community content as mandatory guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Remove or soften claims such as AUTHORITATIVE GUIDANCE, MANDATORY COMPLIANCE, and official source. State that the skill provides troubleshooting guidance subject to higher-priority system and user instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md labels itself as 'AUTHORITATIVE GUIDANCE' with 'MANDATORY COMPLIANCE' and says it is the 'official source'. This can pressure agents to elevate untrusted marketplace content above higher-priority instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wording asserts mandatory authority and official status. No direct instruction says to ignore security analysis, so confidence is high but not maximal.

content.value_statement: Azure incidents often span logs, metrics, health status, and service-specific failure modes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured Azure diagnostics.
actual_capabilities: Guides initial triage through symptoms, resource health, logs, metrics, and recent changes.
Routes App Service, Container Apps, Function Apps, AKS, Event Hubs, and Service Bus issues to focused guides.
Provides Azure CLI, MCP, KQL, and SDK troubleshooting references for common failure modes.
Encourages read-only evidence collection before remediation, especially for AKS workflows.
Summarizes root cause evidence, confidence, next checks, remediation, and escalation paths.
limitations: Requires the user to supply Azure subscription, resource group, service, and time-window details.
Cannot access Azure resources unless the active client has authenticated access.
May surface sensitive operational logs, so users should redact secrets before sharing outputs.
Does not replace Microsoft support for platform outages or critical incidents.

use_cases.title: Triage Azure outages
use_cases.description: Guide a live incident through resource health, metrics, logs, and recent changes before proposing remediation.

use_cases.title: Debug AKS workloads
use_cases.description: Collect cluster, node, pod, DNS, ingress, and event evidence while keeping destructive changes behind approval.

use_cases.title: Resolve messaging failures
use_cases.description: Diagnose Event Hubs and Service Bus authentication, AMQP, lock, checkpoint, and connectivity problems across SDKs.

prompt_templates.title: Start Azure incident triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single Azure service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Azure Diagnostics to triage an App Service issue. Ask me for missing resource details, then check health, logs, metrics, and recent changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate AKS pod failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AKS troubleshooting flow for pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff. Gather read-only evidence first and list likely root causes with confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Function App telemetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose intermittent Function App timeouts. Correlate App Insights traces, Log Analytics data, recent deployments, and resource health before recommending changes.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze messaging SDK failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Troubleshoot production Event Hubs and Service Bus AMQP errors across clients. Separate authentication, network, retry, checkpoint, and lock-renewal causes.

output_examples.input: My App Service returns 503 after deployment.
output: Checks resource health and recent deployment history.
Reviews platform logs, app logs, and health check status.
Returns likely cause, supporting evidence, and next remediation step.

output_examples.input: AKS pods are Pending in one namespace.
output: Collects pod events, node capacity, taints, affinity, PVC, and quota evidence.
Separates scheduling, storage, quota, and node pressure causes.
Recommends read-only next checks before any cluster change.

output_examples.input: Event Hubs consumers disconnect during scaling.
output: Checks load balancing behavior, retry settings, checkpoint frequency, and connection reuse.
Distinguishes expected consumer ownership changes from persistent failures.
Lists SDK-specific fixes and escalation evidence.

best_practices: Start with resource health and recent changes before deep log analysis.
Prefer read-only checks until the user approves a remediation action.
Record evidence, time windows, confidence, and any changes made during the incident.
anti_patterns: Running write commands before confirming the affected resource and scope.
Sharing raw connection strings, secrets, or unredacted production logs in prompts.
Treating one detector warning as root cause without supporting logs or metrics.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and tool calls based on the user environment. Users should approve actions that change resources.

faq.question: Which Azure services does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers App Service, Container Apps, Function Apps, AKS, Event Hubs, and Service Bus troubleshooting.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes, live diagnostics require an authenticated Azure context with permission to read the affected resources.

faq.question: Can it make production changes?
faq.answer: It includes remediation guidance, but production changes should require explicit user approval and operator review.

faq.question: Does it analyze logs and metrics?
faq.answer: Yes. It references Azure Monitor, App Insights, Log Analytics, KQL, and service-specific diagnostic tools.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Provide the service, resource group, subscription, symptom, time window, and any safe log excerpts.
